stories.title: MVP criticizes TNA management for gross mismanagement driving talent away
stories.tldr: During a recent episode of his podcast, current AEW star MVP opened up about his time in TNA Wrestling, blaming the company's historical decline on gross mismanagement and unqualified personnel. He specifically criticized former executive John Gaburick and discussed how backstage incidents involving an intoxicated Gaburick drove top stars like Samoa Joe and Bobby Roode to quit. MVP also pointed to a major missed opportunity when Spike TV reportedly considered buying the promotion years ago but balked at Dixie Carter's involvement and Vince Russo's creative direction.

stories.title: The Bryan & Vinny Show: Zoom Crashout, Mid-South Oct 1984, and Daily Wrestling Topics
stories.tldr: Bryan Alvarez and Vinny ​Roades returned for a new episode of their audio show despite suffering yet another frustrating technical failure on Zoom, which also plagued a separate episode of Wrestling Observer Live hosted by Bryan and Filthy Tom Lawlor. During the flagship show, the hosts engaged in their weekly guilt-ridden chat with Granny—who delivered her usual soap opera and wrestling reports, played trivia, and threatened violence against Bryan—before reviewing an episode of Mid-South Wrestling from October 1984. Meanwhile, the companion Wrestling Observer Live broadcast covered Tom Lawlor nearly injuring himself with a chain during a match, ticket sales updates for Wembley and Dynamite, the major WWE and ESPN story making headlines, and a review of Monday Night Raw.

stories.title: Nic Nemeth thanks WWE star for helping transition to independent scene
stories.tldr: After leaving WWE in September 2023, Nic Nemeth transitioned into the independent wrestling circuit for the first time in his 20-year career. To help navigate this unfamiliar landscape, Nemeth turned to former WWE colleague Matt Cardona, who previously mastered the free agency market and reinvented himself on the indie scene. Nemeth praised Cardona as the blueprint for success, crediting him with essential advice on merchandise and independent operations. Since making the jump, Nemeth has successfully captured championship gold both domestically and internationally.

stories.title: Chris Jericho discussed potential Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling debut
stories.tldr: Chris Jericho recently revealed that he was in talks to appear at the upcoming Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling Northern Rising pay-per-view event. A scheduling conflict ultimately prevented the Canadian wrestling legend from joining the October 3 card at the historic Mattamy Athletic Centre. While Adam Copeland is still set to make his promotional debut on the show, Jericho expressed a strong desire to work with Scott D'Amore and MLP in the future. He praised the company for being a Canadian promotion operated by someone who is smart to the business and operating for the right reasons.

stories.title: Sorgstock live wrestling event set for Bethel, New York
stories.tldr: This Friday, the historic grounds of Bethel, New York, will host Sorgstock, a live wrestling event celebrating the monumental contributions of Pittsburgh video producer Mike Sorg. While Pittsburgh has a rich wrestling history dating back to Bruno Sammartino, Shane Douglas, and Kurt Angle, much of the city is early independent tape library was lost to time due to the high costs of analog production. Through Sorgatron Media, Mike Sorg and his team have revolutionized the region by recording, producing, and livestreaming a modern generation of local grapplers. The upcoming event serves as a tribute to Sorg's decade-plus dedication to preserving and promoting the Steel City independent wrestling scene.

stories.title: Bryan & Vinny & Craig recap TNA Lockdown and AAA coverage
stories.tldr: Vince Verhei breaks down the chaotic aftermath of TNA Lockdown and recent AAA events on the Big Vinny V Show. He questions the confusing booking decisions at TNA Lockdown, including the heavy interference and humiliating babyface losses in the all-cage match gimmick. Additionally, he highlights a bizarre AAA tournament match where neither the advertised competitors nor the actual participants matched who supposedly advanced.

stories.title: JBL comments on Avery Styles controversy prior to TNA signing
stories.tldr: Following his recent TNA signing and upcoming independent debut, Avery Styles has found himself at the center of an online controversy. The discourse stems from an incident where the young wrestler was allegedly asked to help set up an independent show before his match. WWE Hall of Famer JBL has now weighed in on the situation, criticizing the decision to air the dispute publicly and discussing the traditional expectations of paying dues in the wrestling business.

stories.title: Top 10 pro wrestling matches in history on August 25
stories.tldr: Following yesterday's look at historic title changes, attention now turns to the top 10 matches that took place on August 25 across various promotions. Cagematch ratings and Wrestling Observer Newsletter star ratings highlight legendary bouts, topped by Bryan Danielson defeating Swerve Strickland for the AEW title in 2024. Dave Meltzer's detailed review of that 5.25-star main event captures the dramatic, hard-hitting title change.

stories.title: Historical pro wrestling title changes on August 25
stories.tldr: Shifting to the calendar date of August 25, the wrestling archives log roughly 252 notable championship changes over the decades. Key historical milestones on this date feature iconic victories from legends like Sting, Brock Lesnar, and Mickie James. More recent additions to the history books include major title shifts in AAA and Hook capturing the FTW World Heavyweight Title in 2024.

stories.title: Will Ospreay discusses AEW All In main event plans, match against Kenny Omega, and special gear
stories.tldr: Ahead of his AEW World Championship match against Kenny Omega at All In: London, Will Ospreay revealed that AEW considered several alternative directions, including matches with MJF, Jon Moxley, or a triple threat. Ospreay will ditch his traditional green gear for a special red and white kit inspired by England's historic 1966 World Cup victory at Wembley Stadium. He also reflected on the unique sporting legacy of previous All In main events compared to his upcoming generational clash with Omega. If victorious, Ospreay hopes to bring a fresh sports-film mentality to his championship reign.

stories.title: Darby Allin discusses history with Kevin Knight, AEW title reign, and future goals
stories.tldr: In a recent interview, Darby Allin opened up about his history with TNT Champion Kevin Knight ahead of their Falls Count Anywhere match at AEW All In: London, reflecting on how they trained at the same wrestling school and their diverging career paths. Allin also discussed his grueling AEW World Championship win earlier this year, admitting he initially felt numb and physically depleted in the ring before realizing the achievement was entirely uncompromised. Drawing major inspiration from his mentor Sting, Allin stated that he physically and mentally cannot slow down his high-intensity in-ring style and aims to lead by example. Furthermore, he shared his perspective on AEW's evolution since 2019, noting that while some early talent took the company for granted, the current roster features a much higher competitive standard.

stories.title: AEW announces Paris debut with AEW Grand Slam: France
stories.tldr: All Elite Wrestling has officially announced its debut in France with a major special event titled AEW Grand Slam: France, scheduled for Tuesday, October 6, at the Adidas Arena in Paris. The historic show will feature television tapings for both Dynamite and Collision, marking the ninth installment of the company's international Grand Slam series. Tickets are set to go on sale to the general public on Friday, August 28, following early access presale opportunities for registered AEW Insiders. Company leadership and top talent have expressed immense enthusiasm for the market, citing the passionate local fanbase and aiming to establish Paris as a regular hub for live programming.

stories.title: AEW announces Fright Night Dynamite and Collision 2026 in St. Louis
stories.tldr: All Elite Wrestling has announced that St. Louis, Missouri will host the 2026 Fright Night editions of Dynamite and Collision on Wednesday, October 28. The double tapings at Chaifetz Arena continue the promotion's annual Halloween tradition following previous specials in Cleveland and Edinburg. This announcement was part of a larger schedule reveal that also included upcoming stops in Kentucky, Ohio, North Carolina, and a historic debut in Paris, France.

stories.title: AEW Dynamite and Collision schedule update during All Out week
stories.tldr: AEW has announced a unique scheduling change for All Out week, featuring the go-home editions of Dynamite and Collision airing back-to-back on Wednesday, September 23, from Indianapolis. Meanwhile, ticket sales for the post-All In Dynamite in Texas are currently tracking significantly below the year-to-date average. The rest of September largely maintains standard time slots, though future event schedules like October remain fluid.

stories.title: Swerve Strickland praises NXT star Myka Lockwood for using his move
stories.tldr: AEW star Swerve Strickland recently took to social media to praise WWE NXT prospect Myka Lockwood for using a variation of his signature double pumphandle into a falling powerslam. Initially responding with the word influence to a fan comparison video, Strickland later clarified that Lockwood actually utilized the more difficult hand-clutch setup originated by Shane Mercer. He commended her flawless execution of the complex technique, adding to a busy stretch of social media attention for Lockwood following her recent NXT live event powerbomb on CM Punk.

stories.title: AEW All In 2026 ticket sales update and global start times
stories.tldr: AEW All In 2026 is rapidly approaching this weekend at London’s Wembley Stadium on Sunday, August 30, with WrestleTix reporting 41,836 tickets distributed so far. The event features a stacked match card headlined by Kenny Omega defending the AEW World Title against Will Ospreay, alongside global start times adjusted for fans tuning in worldwide. With ticket sales up nearly 1,800 over the last five days and hundreds still available on the resale market, anticipation is at a fever pitch for the company's latest massive UK spectacle.

stories.title: Willow Nightingale on why she joined AEW
stories.tldr: Willow Nightingale recently discussed how All Elite Wrestling has been her dream destination since the company was first founded. She was immediately drawn to its punk rock, alternative approach, which provided a welcoming space that she could not find in WWE. Nightingale credits the promotion for allowing performers to achieve success and find joy by simply being themselves. Now, she is preparing to defend her AEW Women's World Championship against Mercedes Mone at All In at London's Wembley Stadium this Sunday, August 30.

stories.title: MJF says he is out of AEW Grand Slam France
stories.tldr: Former AEW World Champion MJF recently took to social media to state that he is out of the upcoming AEW Grand Slam France event. The company announced it will hold its first-ever show in Paris at the Adidas Arena on October 6, 2026, marking a major milestone in its international expansion. While fans speculated whether the top star would actually miss the show, his brief tweet is widely seen as part of his ongoing heel character work. MJF frequently uses social media to stay in kayfabe, often insulting foreign crowds to generate heat.

stories.title: Kyle Fletcher joke in French interview
stories.tldr: During a French language promotional interview, AEW star Kyle Fletcher accidentally declared himself to be a porn star while attempting to say he was a protostar. He embraced the humorous slip on social media by posting about it ahead of the upcoming AEW Grand Slam France event. Meanwhile, AEW announced its historic debut in Paris at the Adidas Arena scheduled for October 6, 2026. Additionally, Fletcher is currently preparing to defend his AEW International Title in a high stakes match against Konosuke Takeshita and Kazuchika Okada at AEW All In.

stories.title: Mercedes Moné threatens Ric Flair after Charlotte Flair claim
stories.tldr: Following Ric Flair declaring his daughter Charlotte the greatest female wrestler of all time in a social media collage, Mercedes Mone issued a playful threat to the WWE Hall of Famer. Mone warned Flair about getting his ass kicked, while Charlotte responded to her father with an embarrassed reply. Amidst the online banter, Mone is heavily focused on her upcoming match against Willow Nightingale at AEW All In to capture the women's world title.

stories.title: Royce Keys returns on WWE RAW alongside OTM to form new faction
stories.tldr: Royce Keys made a shocking return on Monday Night RAW to close out the show by brutally attacking both teams in the main event alongside the newly called-up NXT tag team OTM, consisting of Bronco Nima and Lucien Price. The trio utilized steel steps and a commentary desk powerbomb to lay waste to The Usos, LA Knight, and Solo Sikoa, standing tall as the broadcast ended. This explosive debut follows Keys' absence from a brutal street fight against Jacob Fatu earlier in the month and Nima's recent departure from the Perros Del Mal faction in AAA.

stories.title: Stephanie Vaquer set for WWE Women's World Championship rematch against Liv Morgan on RAW
stories.tldr: Stephanie Vaquer is officially getting her long-awaited rematch against WWE Women's World Champion Liv Morgan on the September 7 episode of RAW in Birmingham, Alabama. Vaquer earned the title opportunity following a hard-fought victory over Roxanne Perez on the August 24 episode, marking her first match since returning from a four-month injury absence. However, the path to the championship is complicated by the return of Becky Lynch, who saved Vaquer from a post-match ambush by Morgan and set off a tense dynamic between all three competitors.

stories.title: Adam Pearce says he doesn't watch non-WWE wrestling and has no plans to return to the ring
stories.tldr: WWE Raw General Manager Adam Pearce recently revealed in an interview that he does not watch a single minute of professional wrestling outside of WWE, proudly declaring himself a company man who only focuses on the product he helps produce. Despite his background as a legendary independent veteran and five-time NWA World Heavyweight Champion, Pearce stated he has no current interest in keeping up with other promotions. Additionally, when asked if he would follow SmackDown General Manager Nick Aldis back into the ring following Aldis' recent return at SummerSlam, Pearce firmly dismissed the idea. He joked that nobody needs to see a 48-year-old bald man in tights, though he ultimately left the door slightly open by refusing to say never.

stories.title: Joseann Offerman and Mika Rotunda pay tribute to Bray Wyatt on third anniversary of his death
stories.tldr: The wrestling community recently marked the third anniversary of the passing of Bray Wyatt, who died of a heart attack in 2023 at the age of 36. His former wife, Joseann Offerman, shared a deeply emotional social media post reflecting on her lasting grief and raising their children without him. Additionally, Wyatt's sister, Mika Rotunda, posted a heartfelt tribute on Instagram, contrasting the dark characters he played on television with the angel he was in real life. Both tributes highlighted the enduring pain of his loss and the unforgettable legacy he left behind.

stories.title: Drew McIntyre returns to US but WWE return remains uncertain
stories.tldr: Drew McIntyre has officially returned to the United States after a four-month absence following WrestleMania 42. His time away was planned in advance to accommodate outside acting projects, including filming the Highlander reboot alongside Henry Cavill and Russell Crowe, as well as working on The Last Druid in Spain. Despite his return to the country, WWE has not yet started any major creative discussions regarding his television comeback or next storyline. Fans may have to wait a bit longer to see the Scottish Warrior back on screen, though the company's loaded fall schedule offers plenty of opportunities for his eventual return.

stories.title: Steve Austin involved in off-road racing accident
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Stone Cold Steve Austin experienced his first major setback in off-road racing after crashing his Broken Skull Racing vehicle during the Stomping Grounds 300 in Yerington, Nevada. Austin and his co-driver emerged completely uninjured from the incident, despite the car sustaining significant damage that knocked them out of the competition. Although the crash ruined his streak of finishing every race this season, the wrestling legend remains in high spirits and is already repairing the vehicle for the upcoming VC-Tonopah event.

stories.title: Big Cass defeats Je'Von Evans in WWE RAW in-ring return
stories.tldr: Big Cass made his triumphant in-ring return on WWE RAW, defeating Je'Von Evans to secure his first victory for the company in eight years. The match served as the explosive culmination of a recent rivalry that began when Cass attacked Evans earlier in the month following a stint in AEW. Despite a spirited, high-flying offense from Evans that included a springboard lariat and a trip outside into the timekeeper's area, Cass ultimately used his massive size advantage and a devastating big boot to claim the pinfall. Evans' rough night continued after the bell when he was blindsided by The Judgment Day's Dominik Mysterio and JD McDonagh.

stories.title: Haku's surprise WWE SmackDown return was originally planned for July 24
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Haku made a surprise return on the July 31 episode of SmackDown to manage his sons, Tama Tonga and Talla Tonga. However, according to Talla Tonga, the legendary wrestler's comeback was originally scheduled for a week earlier on July 24 in the San Francisco area. WWE ultimately decided to delay the appearance until the week of SummerSlam, allowing them to successfully pull off the surprise broadcast.

stories.title: Oba Femi and Bron Breakker RAW contract signing leads to brawl with Austin Theory
stories.tldr: During the August 24 episode of WWE RAW, Oba Femi and Bron Breakker held a volatile contract signing for Sunday Night's Main Event that quickly turned physical. Femi delivered a fiery promo mocking Breakker as an angry orange man while referencing wrestling legends John Cena and Roman Reigns. After tensions boiled over and Austin Theory interfered on Breakker's behalf, Femi fought off the numbers advantage and put Theory through a table. Femi then officially signed the contract to stand tall and close the segment with the final word.

stories.title: Roman Reigns return announced for August 31 WWE RAW
stories.tldr: WWE has loaded up the August 31 episode of RAW in Charlotte with several major announcements following the August 24 broadcast. The show will feature the highly anticipated return of the Original Tribal Chief Roman Reigns amidst ongoing drama involving The Bloodline, LA Knight, and Solo Sikoa. Additionally, Raquel Rodriguez will defend the Women's Intercontinental Championship against Sol Ruca in a title rematch, and Rey Fenix will battle Penta in the finals of the World Heavyweight Championship Contender Tournament.

stories.title: Jim Cornette blasts Linda McMahon over political remarks
stories.tldr: Veteran wrestling personality Jim Cornette recently lashed out at former WWE CEO and United States Secretary of Education Linda McMahon over political remarks regarding transgender students and parental rights. In a scathing social media post, Cornette labeled McMahon a plastic-faced stooge and referred to Donald Trump, who was standing beside her, as a crime boss while expressing disbelief that anyone believes their claims. Cornette has a long history of publicly criticizing Trump and political figures, demonstrating that his decades-old ties to the wrestling industry will not shield former colleagues from his sharp tongue.

stories.title: Cody Rhodes heel turn discussion and comparisons to Hulk Hogan
stories.tldr: Recent speculation about a potential heel turn for Cody Rhodes has intensified following promos hinting at him no longer being the nice guy and his use of Paul Heyman's signature catchphrase. Wrestling analysts have weighed in by comparing the potential magnitude of Cody turning to the dark side to Hulk Hogan joining the NWO at Bash at the Beach in 1996. Observers have floated several potential scenarios for the turn, including aligning with Paul Heyman, becoming a corporate champion under The Rock, forming an elite faction of former rivals, or brutally retiring Randy Orton.

stories.title: Jordynne Grace writing research paper on NXT female vs male athlete performance
stories.tldr: WWE star Jordynne Grace is channeling a heavily debated NXT topic into an academic research paper for her kinesiology class, exploring why female athletes frequently outperform their male counterparts during developmental training. The discussion was notably sparked by comments from Grayson Waller and Kevin Owens regarding the women's division running laps around the men. Grace's study highlights key factors such as skill-based sports transferability, precision coaching experience, and a recruitment focus on size for men versus skill for women. Meanwhile, Grace has been absent from SmackDown television since April, balancing her studies with occasional Main Event bouts, dark matches, and outside pursuits like her pilot license application.

stories.title: WWE RAW August 24, 2026 ticket sales update and start time
stories.tldr: WWE RAW emanates from the Canadian Tire Centre in Ottawa with an early start time to accommodate back-to-back SmackDown tapings. Over 8,300 tickets have been distributed, beating the venue's previous attendance figures from 2024. The live broadcast features a loaded card including multiple tournament matches and a contract signing.

stories.title: John Cena explains his evolving WWE role following retirement
stories.tldr: John Cena has officially retired from in-ring competition but remains dedicated to the WWE family. During a recent podcast appearance, he explained that his post-retirement role is still a work in progress as he figures out his new corporate persona. He emphasized that he will never wrestle again, adopting a new wardrobe to ensure fans know he now operates as a promoter and spokesperson rather than an active competitor.

stories.title: WWE RAW August 24, 2026 review
stories.tldr: The August 24, 2026 episode of Monday Night Raw featured major NXT call-ups including OTM and Lola Vice, alongside the semifinals of the World Heavyweight Championship number one contender tournament. Reviewers had mixed reactions, heavily criticizing Big Cass in-ring return match against Je'Von Evans and the commentary team treatment of him. On the positive side, fans and critics alike praised the fast-paced, high-flying semifinal bout between Rey Fenix and Dragon Lee that set up a finals clash between the Lucha Brothers.

stories.title: CM Punk and AJ Lee reflect on passing of dog Larry
stories.tldr: WWE stars CM Punk and AJ Lee opened up about the passing of their beloved dog, Larry, during the third season of Netflix series WWE Unreal. Larry, a rescue dog adopted in 2015 who had a bite record, became a central part of the couple's family for a decade. Punk famously wore a Larry's Dad patch at Survivor Series 2025 shortly after the dog's death, and Larry has since been immortalized as an action figure by Mattel.

stories.title: Speculation on old WWE Championship belts returning
stories.tldr: As WWE continues to evolve across its main roster and developmental brands, speculation has grown regarding the potential return of several retired or unused championship belts. From NXT staples like the Heritage Cup and the NXT Women's Tag Team Championship to unique concepts like the Evolve Tag Team Championship and the People's Championship, various divisions could soon see new gold introduced. Additionally, leveraging the recent AAA acquisition might pave the way for a WWE-wide Cruiserweight Championship. These potential re-introductions aim to bolster divisions that currently lack secondary or tag team representation.

stories.title: Baron Corbin and former WWE stars expected to re-sign
stories.tldr: Recent months have seen several familiar faces return to WWE, highlighted by Baron Corbin winning the United States Championship and Big Cass making a dominant return. This trend suggests WWE may look to its past even more heading toward 2027, with potential re-signings including FTR, Enzo Amore, Donovan Dijak, and Braun Strowman. Speculation surrounds whether these former stars could make major impacts in tag team or singles divisions under the current creative regime.

stories.title: Nikki Bella speaks candidly on dating and sex after divorce
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Nikki Bella recently opened up on her podcast about her current perspective on dating, relationships, and sex following her divorce. She shared that she is completely at peace with the possibility of remaining single forever and no longer feels a need for a partner to feel fulfilled. However, she remains open to future romance, noting that she still desires affection, shared quiet evenings, and great sex when the time is right.

stories.title: Trick Williams reflects on US Championship loss compliment
stories.tldr: Former United States Champion Trick Williams recently reflected on losing his title to Baron Corbin at SummerSlam after a 105-day reign. Although fans were frustrated by the decision, Williams viewed the hostile crowd reaction as the biggest compliment to his work. He explained that making the room go silent when losing the belt proved he is successfully connecting with the audience and leaving an impact. Williams is now looking to reclaim the championship, though his next opportunity depends on Lil Yachty surviving a five-minute match against Corbin at Sunday Night's Main Event.

stories.title: WWE LFG Season 3 finale date and details announced
stories.tldr: A and E has announced that the season finale of WWE LFG Season Three will air on Sunday, September 6th, at 10:01 PM ET. Titled What Happened in Vegas, the finale follows the penultimate episode airing at 9 PM ET on the same night. The episode will showcase four finalists performing at WWE World during WrestleMania Week as they compete for NXT contracts and looming call-ups. The current season premiered in late April and features coaching from Kevin Owens, Nattie, Booker T, and Bully Ray.

stories.title: WON Flashback: Kane vs The Great Khali at WWE SummerSlam 2009
stories.tldr: This retrospective looks back at the infamous match between Kane and The Great Khali at WWE SummerSlam 2009. The author humorously corrects a previous timeline error regarding Daniel Bryan before diving into Dave Meltzer's scathing review of the bout. Meltzer famously awarded the sluggish encounter a minus-one star rating, highlighting the dead crowd and terrible brawling. Despite the universally panned quality, the feud bizarrely continued on television afterward.

stories.title: CM Punk wears Iyo Sky entrance robe at WWE live event
stories.tldr: CM Punk continued his recent trend of wearing the entrance gear of fellow WWE Superstars during a live event in Calgary. At the August 23rd show, he walked out wearing Iyo Sky's signature robe to the delight of the fans. To complete the tribute, Punk also recreated Sky's distinct signature entrance pose in the ring. The lighthearted moment quickly circulated on social media via fan-captured video clips.

stories.title: Penta vs. Rey Fenix set for World Heavyweight Title Contender Tournament finals on WWE RAW
stories.tldr: The WWE World Heavyweight Championship contender tournament has reached its final stage following the semifinal matches on Raw. Rey Fenix defeated Dragon Lee and Penta defeated La Parka to advance. The brothers will now square off in the tournament finals next week, with the winner earning a title match against Roman Reigns in Mexico City.

stories.title: Lola Vice main roster call-up date teased on WWE RAW
stories.tldr: Despite earlier expectations pointing toward SmackDown, Lola Vice is officially heading to the red brand for her main roster debut. A new vignette aired on Monday Night Raw revealing that the former NXT star will arrive on September 14. That debut will take place live from Mexico City as Vice transitions away from her developmental run.

stories.title: Hiromu Takahashi (Kyoki) wrestles dark match prior to WWE RAW after debuting on SmackDown
stories.tldr: Former New Japan star Hiromu Takahashi recently debuted on SmackDown under the ring name Kyoki as Shinsuke Nakamura's mystery partner. Following that initial introduction, Kyoki quickly transitioned to in-ring action by wrestling his very first match under the WWE banner. He competed in a dark match prior to Monday Night RAW in Ottawa, picking up a victory over Kit Wilson.

stories.title: Tony Khan, AJ Styles, and wrestling personalities comment on Ilja Dragunov leaving WWE
stories.tldr: Following his departure from WWE, free agent Ilja Dragunov is drawing heavy speculation regarding a move to AEW or potential European independent dates. AEW President Tony Khan recently addressed the rumors, praising Dragunov as a tremendous talent while remaining non-committal about current negotiations. In new comments, Khan doubled down on his praise and stated he will always be on the lookout for the star's next move. Meanwhile, WWE star AJ Styles admitted he was shocked and saddened by Dragunov leaving the company.

stories.title: Johnny Gargano WWE departure rumors addressed
stories.tldr: Johnny Gargano sparked fresh departure rumors by posting a nostalgic return video on social media and fueling internet speculation about his Twitter bio. However, sources confirm he remains under WWE contract and listed on the internal roster. His recent absence from television stems from a combination of a catatonic backstage storyline on SmackDown and a personal family leave following his father's Stage 4 cancer diagnosis.

stories.title: WWE tag team division revival plans
stories.tldr: WWE is leaning on several fresh duos and unexpected alliances to rebuild its depleted tag team ranks. Plans feature Shinsuke Nakamura partnering with debuting star Kyoki, alongside new pairings like Ethan Page and Rusev. Other highlighted acts include a potential Dragon Lee and Je'Von Evans team, Bronson Reed rejoining Bron Breakker, and the eventual arrival of the Lucha Bros.

stories.title: Missa Kate attends TNA Lockdown and addresses potential in-ring return
stories.tldr: Former NWA star Missa Kate was recently spotted attending TNA Lockdown in her hometown of Chicago, Illinois. Having retired from professional wrestling late last year following a career-versus-career match, she has now addressed her future in the sport. Kate revealed that she maintains a never-say-never mindset regarding a potential in-ring return, leaving the door open for a future comeback.

stories.title: Daily Update: Paramount-WBD lawsuit talks, Vince McMahon birthday, dark matches
stories.tldr: Settlement talks between Warner Bros Discovery, Paramount Skydance, and twelve state attorney generals have been called off following a dispute over leaked confidential information to the Wall Street Journal. The uncertain merger creates potential fallout for All Elite Wrestling, though Tony Khan reportedly remains optimistic about working with David Ellison and maintaining synergy across TBS, TNT, and HBO Max. Meanwhile, the professional wrestling world continues to navigate a busy news cycle featuring roster updates, upcoming pay-per-view events, historical retrospectives, and television schedule changes.

stories.title: Moose explains Triple H tribute entrance at TNA Lockdown
stories.tldr: Following TNA Lockdown 2026, Moose explained that his elaborate throne entrance was a direct homage to WWE executive and legend Triple H, whom he grew up watching. During the event in Chicago, Moose faced Frankie Kazarian inside a steel cage in a match featuring escape the cage rules. The unique finish saw Moose hit a spear that accidentally knocked Kazarian through the door to the outside, handing Kazarian the victory despite being laid out. Moose later shared on social media that mimicking Triple H's larger than life WrestleMania entrances was a dream tribute, capping off a period that also saw Moose fulfill a career goal by competing in NXT during 2025 through the TNA and WWE crossover partnership.

stories.title: JCW Lunacy announces major schedule change
stories.tldr: JCW has announced a major schedule change for its weekly Lunacy program, moving this week's broadcast away from its traditional Thursday night slot. Instead, the promotion will air a special live episode on Saturday, August 29, beginning at 8:00 PM Eastern. The company issued multiple reminders to ensure fans do not tune in on the wrong night. While no specific reasons or match card details were provided for the shift, viewers will simply need to wait a couple of extra days to catch the action.

stories.title: Eddie Kingston to challenge Hechicero for CMLL World Heavyweight Championship
stories.tldr: AEW star Eddie Kingston is set to make his official debut for CMLL on August 28, 2026, where he will challenge Hechicero for the CMLL World Heavyweight Championship. This booking also strongly indicates that Kingston has been medically cleared to return to action, following a previous health issue that forced him to withdraw from the AEW Continental Cup Challenge. The high-profile event at Arena Mexico will also feature a World Tag Team Title Qualifier match between Villanos, Dinastía Panther, and Gemelos Diablo.

stories.title: WOL: Nick Wayne vs Bandido, Punk vs Owens, and weekend news
stories.tldr: Wrestling Observer Live returned with host Bryan Alvarez and special guest host Royce Isaacs for an episode packed with wrestling news and event previews. The hosts dove into upcoming matches including the exciting clash between Nick Wayne and Bandido. They also previewed Friday Night Smackdown featuring a marquee matchup between Kevin Owens and CM Punk, alongside a thorough review of the weekend news.

stories.title: Dustin Rhodes, Brian James, and political commentary in wrestling
stories.tldr: Dustin Rhodes recently faced severe online backlash after reacting positively to a controversial, Islamophobic social media post featuring an armed woman. Following public criticism from TNA wrestler Mustafa Ali, Dustin issued an apology citing selective reading before locking his account. This incident underscores the ongoing friction when professional wrestlers blend personal political views with public social media engagement.

stories.title: Pro Wrestling NOAH's Midori Takahashi out with shoulder injury
stories.tldr: Pro Wrestling NOAH performer Midori Takahashi is currently sidelined of action due to a dislocated shoulder. This injury will force Takahashi to miss the promotion's upcoming live events on August 29 and August 30. Takahashi's most recent appearance took place on August 23 at the NOAH Kawasaki Summer Voyage show.

stories.title: This Day in Wrestling History: August 24 title changes
stories.tldr: August 24 holds a significant place in professional wrestling history, having hosted 275 notable title changes over the decades. The timeline features legendary moments ranging from early tag team victories in the 1960s to modern championships won across various promotions up to 2025. Major historical highlights include championship wins by icons like Ricky Steamboat, the Steiner Brothers, and El Dandy.

stories.title: Angel Garza defends AAA Los Perros del Mal storyline against fan criticism
stories.tldr: Angel Garza recently criticized impatient fans for complaining about the Los Perros del Mal storyline in AAA. In addition to Garza's comments, fellow WWE star Karmen Petrovic publicly weighed in on the social media exchange to back him up. The storyline itself featured Penta defeating Bronco Nima under a stipulation that would have forced Penta into the faction, followed by a post-match melee involving Rey Fenix and Dragon Lee, and Nima subsequently being kicked out of the group.

stories.title: WWE wrestler Bayley and other stars spotted backstage at TNA Lockdown
stories.tldr: Independent wrestlers J-Rod and Josh Bishop were recently spotted at TNA Lockdown following WWE tryouts. They were joined at the Chicago event by WWE superstar Bayley, who has been absent from television since July. Several other independent and developmental talents, including Pinky Montoya, Kal Herro, and Missa Kate, were also present backstage.

stories.title: TNA Rosemary injury and return status update
stories.tldr: Rosemary is facing an extended recovery period following an injury suffered at an independent event. Because of her absence, Kiera Hogan recently returned as Allie's partner at TNA Lockdown to successfully defend the Knockouts World Tag Team Championship. However, backstage reports indicate that Hogan is not a permanent replacement, and fans should not expect Rosemary back in the ring anytime soon.

stories.title: Avery Styles signs with TNA Wrestling and debuts at Lockdown
stories.tldr: Following his major contract signing and debut at the TNA Lockdown pay-per-view, Avery Styles is wasting no time expanding his schedule. The son of AJ Styles has officially been announced for his upcoming independent debut with ETU Wrestling. He is set to compete at the All I Want 4 event on September 19 in New Jersey. This booking marks the teenager's first major independent appearance since locking down his new TNA deal.

stories.title: Aleister Black (Malakai Black) teased for UK PROGRESS Wrestling event
stories.tldr: Malakai Black is already set for a PROGRESS Wrestling return in September, and new company owner Big Damo has heavily teased an additional appearance later that month. Damo pointed fans toward the September 27 When September Ends event in London on social media. This cryptic tease strongly hints that the star may perform under his former Tommy End moniker for the Camden Ballroom show.

stories.title: AAA TripleMania expanding to two nights in Las Vegas
stories.tldr: AAA is expanding TripleMania 34 to a historic two-night format across Las Vegas and Mexico City on September 11 and 13. While TKO pushes to secure a permanent American television deal for AAA beyond YouTube, the ambitious weekend schedule is causing significant strain on WWE production staff and talent. Wrestlers pulling double duty across the events face a grueling workload that deviates from standard booking practices.

stories.title: Wrestling Observer Radio: Weekend news, ROH, TNA, SmackDown, and Collision
stories.tldr: The latest audio update expands on a busy weekend of professional wrestling with extensive news coverage. Matt Cardona is sidelined with a torn triceps, and Warner Bros Discovery settlement talks are reportedly set to begin soon. The program also reviews major weekend events from ROH and TNA, addresses roster updates like Avery Styles signing, and covers recent television episodes.

stories.title: Mercedes Moné responds to Ric Flair calling Charlotte Flair the female GOAT
stories.tldr: Ric Flair recently took to Instagram to declare his daughter Charlotte Flair the greatest female wrestler of all time while sharing a photo collage that also featured Trish Stratus, AJ Lee, Stephanie McMahon, and Mercedes Mone. Mone, who was included in the collage from her days as Sasha Banks, quickly fired back at the Nature Boy in the comments section. Playfully threatening the WWE Hall of Famer, Mone challenged his bold claim by asking if he wanted to get his ass kicked while throwing in his signature woooo.

stories.title: Paige (Saraya) calls out weird airport scalper behavior
stories.tldr: Saraya, formerly known as Paige, recently called out an aggressive airport scalper who purchased a plane ticket just to ambush her at a connecting flight gate with dozens of photos to sign. The wrestling star condemned the tactic as invasive behavior, joining a growing list of talent speaking out against merchandise resellers at travel hubs. The incident highlights an increasing trend where scalpers buy tickets to bypass security and exploit wrestlers during their travels.

stories.title: AEW Brawl In The Ballpark special event streaming details
stories.tldr: All Elite Wrestling is streaming its special event, Brawl In The Ballpark, tonight at 6 pm ET worldwide and ad-free via the MyAEW platform. The broadcast features the action from the July 10, 2026, live event hosted by the Minnesota Twins at Target Field in Minneapolis. Fans can tune in to hear commentary from Ian Riccaboni and Tony Schiavone calling matches such as Orange Cassidy versus Wheeler Yuta and The Hurt Syndicate versus Shane Taylor Promotions.

stories.title: AEW production and entrance limitations for All In London at Wembley Stadium
stories.tldr: AEW is gearing up for its major All In London pay-per-view event at Wembley Stadium on Sunday, August 30, 2026, featuring extravagant entrances for top talent. Despite plans for impressive displays from stars like Mercedes Mone, Will Ospreay, and Kenny Omega, the company will face strict limitations on pyrotechnics. This restriction comes in the wake of a wildfire risk controversy at the stadium involving a recent concert held during a severe UK government weather alert. Local authorities have since sought strict assurances from venue officials regarding safety and fire management.

stories.title: Deonna Purrazzo praises Steph De Lander following ROH Death Before Dishonor match
stories.tldr: Following her successful ROH Women's Pure Title defense at ROH Death Before Dishonor, Deonna Purrazzo expressed high praise for her opponent, Steph De Lander. During the post-show media scrum, Purrazzo highlighted De Lander's decision to bet on herself by leaving her previous company and praised her resilience following neck surgery. Purrazzo emphasized her passion for supporting women in wrestling and stated she was honored to introduce De Lander's talents to the Ring of Honor audience.

stories.title: Reason behind AEW Dynamite's lengthy television overruns revealed
stories.tldr: Recent AEW Dynamite broadcasts have frequently run well past their scheduled ending times, sparking curiosity and backstage debate. According to reports, network partner Warner Bros. Discovery specifically requests these extended overruns to secure extra programming content. While some talent and staff within AEW have expressed frustration over the uncompensated extra time and declining viewership at the end of the show, Tony Khan continues to accommodate the network. Ultimately, keeping WBD happy is a strategic move for AEW as they look toward the network's 2028 option on their television deal.

stories.title: Jeff Jarrett shares career advice for his younger self
stories.tldr: AEW veteran Jeff Jarrett recently reflected on what wisdom he would share with his younger self during an episode of his My World podcast. Prompted by a recent interview question, Jarrett emphasized the importance of embracing love and appreciating life struggles. Drawing from a lifetime of personal and professional trials, including founding TNA, personal loss, and recovery, the 59-year-old wrestling star noted that life valleys are essential for creating mountaintops.

stories.title: Dax Harwood credits WWE NXT match for starting FTR's tag team momentum
stories.tldr: While currently on a wrestling hiatus, AEW star Dax Harwood reflected on his career and pinpointed a specific 2016 match as the catalyst for FTR's success. He credited their NXT TakeOver: Dallas clash against American Alpha for truly establishing them on the brand. Harwood also highlighted his enduring mutual respect and ongoing relationship with Chad Gable.

stories.title: Wrestling Observer Live discusses AEW, ROH title reigns, and Bayley
stories.tldr: The latest episode of Wrestling Observer Live dives into the challenges facing All Elite Wrestling, including a lackluster crowd at Collision and the slow build toward the upcoming All In pay-per-view. The discussion also explores the future of midcard talent like Daniel Garcia amidst expected new roster signings and argues for shorter championship reigns in Ring of Honor. Additionally, the show touches on Bayley's recent career decisions, previews TNA Lockdown, and covers various personal and pop culture topics.

stories.title: Former WWE stars rumored to debut in AEW All In Casino Gauntlet Match
stories.tldr: AEW's upcoming All In pay-per-view features the Casino Gauntlet Match, which serves as an ideal platform for major surprise debuts. With several notable names recently leaving WWE, analysts are speculating on who might enter the match as a surprise entrant. Potential candidates include top-tier free agents like Ilja Dragunov and Sheamus, legacy names like Davey Boy Smith Jr, and independent standouts such as Joseph Sawyer and Malakai Black.

stories.title: MJF appearance and additional matches announced for AEW Dynamite
stories.tldr: MJF will appear live on the upcoming episode of AEW Dynamite in Glasgow following his translator's message to Andrade last week. AEW National Champion Andrade El Idolo is also scheduled to speak on the show. These developments build toward their number one and number two entry spots in the Casino Gauntlet match at AEW All In.

stories.title: Matt Cardona suffers torn tricep injury at WWE Main Event taping
stories.tldr: WWE star Matt Cardona has announced that he suffered a torn tricep during a match against Kit Wilson at a Main Event taping in Toronto. Despite the injury, Cardona remains determined, noting on social media that he still hit the gym to work on his legs and is not finished yet. The setback adds to a rough month for the Cardona household, coming shortly after his wife, Chelsea Green, suffered a broken orbital bone. How WWE will handle his absence and the exact recovery timeline remain unclear as of this writing.

stories.title: ESPN Unlimited increases subscription prices affecting WWE PLE viewers
stories.tldr: ESPN has announced a price increase for its streaming tiers, directly impacting WWE fans who rely on the platform to watch Premium Live Events. Starting September 17, the monthly ESPN Unlimited subscription will rise from $29.99 to $31.99, while the annual plan will increase from $299.99 to $319.99. Additionally, the lower-tier ESPN Select service is also seeing price bumps for both monthly and annual options. This latest adjustment makes one of the most expensive major sports streaming packages even costlier for professional wrestling viewers.

stories.title: Fabian Aichner opens up about WWE release following dropped character vignettes
stories.tldr: Former WWE star Fabian Aichner recently opened up on Busted Open Radio about the emotional roller coaster of his sudden release following a series of dropped return vignettes as Giovanni Vinci. Aichner recalled receiving the unexpected phone call by his pool just as he thought his career-defining moment was finally arriving. After wrestling his final WWE match in December 2025 and briefly stepping away from the industry to experience life without wrestling, he has since successfully resurfaced in TNA as of May 2026.

stories.title: Joe Hendry responds to negative fan reaction over WWE Raw segment with Danhausen
stories.tldr: Joe Hendry recently addressed the significant online criticism surrounding his and Danhausen's concert segment on WWE Raw last July. Appearing on Busted Open, Hendry opened up about the backlash, admitting that missing the mark can be painful when he strives so hard to give fans value. He emphasized his total commitment to WWE, detailing how he moved to Orlando to immerse himself in NXT classes and local shows. Looking past the negative reception, Hendry remains focused on working hard, learning from the highest level of professional wrestling, and continuing to deliver his absolute best to the audience.

stories.title: Bryan & Vinny Show recaps SmackDown and Collision
stories.tldr: The latest episode of the Bryan and Vinny Show delivers a comprehensive recap of the week in professional wrestling. Hosts break down the highlights from Friday Night SmackDown, which featured a stellar main event between CM Punk and Kevin Owens. The review also covers Saturday Collision featuring Continental Cup matches and ongoing build toward Wembley. Additionally, the hosts strongly urge listeners to seek out and watch the standout match between Nick Wayne and Bandido.

stories.title: Fan hits WWE-style dropkick during upper deck brawl at White Sox game
stories.tldr: During a White Sox versus Mets game, a massive brawl erupted in the upper deck involving multiple fans throwing punches and shoves. Escalating the chaos, one individual launched a full-on wrestling-style dropkick that sent another fan crashing backward through the rows. Security eventually restored order, though the viral ringside-style incident overshadowed the White Sox dramatic ninth-inning walk-off victory on the field.

stories.title: Booker T recalls concerns over fan acceptance of a Black World Champion
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Booker T recently reflected on winning his first WCW World Heavyweight Championship at Bash at the Beach in 2000. He admitted he was deeply worried about whether wrestling fans would accept a Black man in that top role, especially considering the lack of sustained main event pushes for predecessors like Ron Simmons. Beyond fan reception, Booker T also noted that navigating the intense backstage politics and the good old boy system of that era presented major hurdles. Despite these apprehensions, he went on to capture the WCW World Heavyweight Championship multiple times, eventually becoming the final wrestler to hold the title before the company was sold to WWE.

stories.title: Rob Van Dam discusses broken WWE promises during his run
stories.tldr: Rob Van Dam recently opened up about his early WWE run, revealing that constant backstage disappointment led him to stop believing management's plans. Despite working immediately with top stars like The Rock and Chris Jericho, RVD felt that unfulfilled promises outweighed his actual television success. He noted that broken commitments, such as suffering a frustrating loss to Luther Reigns during a major WWE trip to Japan, left a lasting negative impression. Consequently, RVD remembers the dashed expectations more vividly than historic victories over legends like Kurt Angle and The Rock.

stories.title: Report details high WWE NXT contracts matching main-roster money
stories.tldr: Recent reports reveal that select WWE NXT talent are already earning main-roster level money before ever moving to Raw or SmackDown. Major names like Jordynne Grace, Joe Hendry, and potentially Ricky Starks and Ethan Page have signed deals exceeding the $350,000 main-roster minimum. Because these wrestlers already command high salaries to add value for the CW Network, WWE does not automatically issue new contracts or reset their timelines upon a main-roster call-up.

stories.title: Hulk Hogan reflects on iconic rivalry and betrayal by Andre the Giant
stories.tldr: Hulk Hogan reflects on one of the most iconic rivalries in professional wrestling history, focusing on the historic betrayal by Andre the Giant. In a special feature from the WWE Vault, the legendary champion tells all about the events leading up to their legendary clash. The in-depth look explores the deep emotions and immense impact of Andre turning his back on his longtime friend. This retrospective provides fans with a behind the scenes perspective on a defining moment in sports entertainment.

stories.title: WWE star debuts new hair look following championship loss and heel turn teases
stories.tldr: Following a recent loss of the Women’s United States Championship on SmackDown due to miscommunication with Chelsea Green, WWE star Tiffany Stratton has debuted a striking new pink hair look on TikTok. The championship defeat and subsequent tension have sparked strong speculation of an impending heel turn against Green, mirroring the villainous persona that defined her successful rise in NXT and her early main roster days. Fans and analysts believe this character shift could reignite her momentum and position her for a major championship pursuit upon Rhea Ripley's eventual return from injury.

stories.title: Eric Bischoff discusses struggling with 'What?' chants upon entering WWE
stories.tldr: Eric Bischoff recently discussed on his podcast how difficult it was to handle the famous What chants when he first arrived in WWE as an on-screen authority figure. He noted that the chants, popularized by Stone Cold Steve Austin, were weaponized by fans to throw performers off their game during promos. Bischoff viewed the phenomenon as an early sign of crowds realizing their immense power to influence live television. Even Steve Austin has reportedly felt some guilt over how the chant has endured and complicated his legacy.

stories.title: Natalya reflects on 1997 Canadian Stampede ahead of WWE return to Calgary
stories.tldr: Ahead of WWE returning to Calgary for a house show at the Saddledome, Natalya shared a nostalgic throwback to the historic 1997 In Your House: Canadian Stampede pay-per-view. In her social media post, the veteran wrestler reflected on being just 15 years old when she joined the Hart Foundation celebration in the ring, marking the last time her legendary family was all together in a WWE ring. Natalya expressed her deep gratitude for returning to the exact same venue where her journey began, coinciding with WWE's current multi-city Canadian tour.

stories.title: WWE star claims wrestling fans would 'suck as writers'
stories.tldr: WWE star Angel Garza recently criticized fans on social media after they backlash over a recent angle involving Los Perros del Mal in AAA. Garza argued that viewers would make terrible writers because they are too impatient and want to rush straight to the climax of a story in a single show. The controversy stems from Bronco Nima being swiftly booted from the faction after losing to Penta, leaving an open spot in the group. Speculation is now growing that former World Heavyweight Champion Damian Priest could soon fill the vacancy following his recent AAA debut.

stories.title: Natalya discusses plans for opening a Hart Family Dungeon training school
stories.tldr: WWE star Natalya recently discussed the potential of eventually opening the legendary Hart Family Dungeon training school to the general public. Currently, the modern iteration of the school operates strictly on an invite-only basis and is led by Natalya and her husband, TJ Wilson. Natalya emphasized that they do not charge trainees, choosing instead to personally fund the facility while prioritizing absolute dedication and passion for the professional wrestling business.

stories.title: Status update on Johnny Gargano amid WWE absence and rumors
stories.tldr: Johnny Gargano has not wrestled in WWE since the April 17, 2026 edition of SmackDown, leading to fan speculation about his status when some noticed his Twitter bio did not mention the company. However, wrestling sources clarified that Gargano has not had WWE in his bio for years and remains firmly on the internal roster. Rumors were further fueled by former creative team member Road Dogg Brian James, who posted a cryptic message on Facebook about changing times and Gargano's association with Triple H.

stories.title: Backstage producers revealed for recent WWE Raw episode
stories.tldr: WWE recently hosted an action-packed episode of Monday Night RAW in Buffalo, New York, featuring major stars, tournament action, and championship matches. Internal reports have now revealed the backstage producers responsible for orchestrating each segment and bout on the card. The broadcast, which carried the internal title Delivered, highlighted top talent across multiple divisions including heavy-hitting faction confrontations.

stories.title: Tyson Kidd reflects on transitioning from WWE wrestler to backstage producer
stories.tldr: Former WWE star Tyson Kidd recently reflected on his transition from an in-ring competitor to a backstage producer following his career-ending injury in 2015. Speaking on Busted Open Radio, Kidd shared that his producer role is even more fulfilling than his wrestling career, despite the challenge of having to coach talent entirely verbally rather than showing them in the ring. Nic Nemeth also appeared on the show to praise Kidd for bringing fresh ideas and benefiting the entire roster during his early days behind the scenes. Kidd credited Nemeth, Seth Rollins, and Finn Balor for helping him navigate the unguided transition into his new backstage role.

stories.title: Amazing Red recalls 2005 WWE dark match against CM Punk
stories.tldr: During a recent appearance on Chris Van Vliet Insight, Amazing Red reflected on his lone 2005 WWE dark match against CM Punk, which served as a crucial tryout for Punk under the supervision of agent Ricky Steamboat. Red faced immense pressure backstage after learning it was potentially Punk's last chance to get signed, while also being told he could not use his signature high-flying moves. The match itself suffered from botches and miscommunication, leading to a blunt backstage critique from John Laurinaitis about Red looking blown up. Although Red never got to thank Punk that night due to Punk walking away, he has since moved past the bitter experience.

stories.title: Lainey Reid describes bittersweet feeling regarding her WWE NXT call-up
stories.tldr: Lainey Reid recently discussed the bittersweet nature of her rapid WWE main roster call-up to SmackDown alongside Fallon Henley and Jacy Jayne. Although reaching the main roster is the ultimate goal for developmental talent, Reid felt she missed out on accomplishing several personal ambitions in NXT due to the timing. However, she has embraced a fresh mindset, viewing the transition as an opportunity to introduce herself to a broader audience without prior expectations.

stories.title: Matt Hardy recalls Vince McMahon scrapping Bray Wyatt match plans late at night
stories.tldr: Matt Hardy recently revealed that Vince McMahon late at night scrapped his elaborate cinematic match plans against the late Bray Wyatt in 2018. Hardy had envisioned a high-risk spot involving a tree, stacked tables, and a supernatural appearance by the ghost of Brother Nero. However, after hours of waiting, production finally heard back from McMahon at 2 a.m. with orders to halt the cinematic stunts and pivot to a live finish instead.

stories.title: Seth Rollins' expected plans for WWE return following SummerSlam
stories.tldr: Seth Rollins has been off WWE television since losing to Roman Reigns at SummerSlam 2026 Night Two, leaving creative with a blank slate for his eventual return. Potential directions for the former Shield member include entering the Money in the Bank ladder match to chase a historic back-to-back briefcase win or assisting Oba Femi against The Vision. Other options involve a brand switch to SmackDown for fresh matchups or reigniting past rivalries with stars like Drew McIntyre.

stories.title: WWE star teases returning to previous character persona
stories.tldr: Johnny Gargano has spent months inactive and struggling with depression on WWE television following major setbacks like losing a feud and his tag partner moving to AEW. Fueling speculation of a character change, he recently marked the anniversary of his 2022 return with a cryptic social media post. This comes as a broader reminder that only a tiny fraction of Triple H's 2022 wave of rehires remain with the company today.

stories.title: Bayley and Blake Monroe exchange social media teases regarding WWE future
stories.tldr: Bayley and Blake Monroe have escalated their social media feud, with Monroe directly challenging Bayley to appear on this week's SmackDown. The interaction coincides with Bayley celebrating her tenth main roster anniversary and exchanging cryptic messages with Raw General Manager Adam Pearce. Meanwhile, frequent television mentions by Lyra Valkyria and backstage reports suggest WWE management expects the veteran star to return.

stories.title: Update on WWE main roster call-up plans and vignettes for Lola Vice
stories.tldr: Lola Vice's upcoming SmackDown arrival features newly filmed vignettes that are described as attention-grabbing and expected to begin airing in the coming weeks. Reports indicate she will land on the Friday night brand alongside her real-life boyfriend Damian Priest. Additional details have also emerged regarding her recent championship run in NXT and her final appearances in AAA.

stories.title: Natalya comments on Chelsea Green's injury and Solo Sikoa's babyface potential
stories.tldr: Natalya recently argued that Chelsea Green's broken orbital bone is a blessing in disguise, providing an organic storyline obstacle that keeps fans hooked during her interim championship reign. Green successfully convinced Nick Aldis to let her keep the title following an emotional promo, earning support from colleagues including her husband Matt Cardona. Additionally, Natalya predicted that Solo Sikoa is positioned to become WWE's next major babyface due to his evolving personality and growing fan connection.

stories.title: Jim Johnston criticized over comments regarding source of pro wrestling theme songs
stories.tldr: Legendary composer Jim Johnston recently sparked debate by arguing that using commercial licensed songs for wrestler entrance themes is a mistake. He believes pop or rock tracks distract fans by tying personal memories to the music instead of focusing entirely on the wrestler. Critics of his viewpoint note that many iconic wrestling moments have successfully relied on famous commercial tracks over the years.

stories.title: Backstage update on WWE's primary objectives for non-televised house shows
stories.tldr: WWE is pushing its roster to create viral social media moments during live events rather than sticking to traditional house show matches. This strategy is a key focus of the ongoing 2026 Summer Tour, which spans multiple continents and features unexpected wrestler pairings. Recent untelevised shows have highlighted this approach through unusual tag team combinations and comedic or aggressive segments involving top stars like CM Punk, Cody Rhodes, Kevin Owens, and Danhausen.

stories.title: Chelsea Green explains why on-screen pairing with Matt Cardona was inevitable
stories.tldr: Chelsea Green recently debuted a custom bedazzled face mask and has been making chaotic waves on SmackDown. In a new interview, she opened up about finally sharing an on-screen WWE segment with her real-life husband, Matt Cardona. Cardona recently returned to defend her from Gunther on television, which Green noted was an inevitable blending of their real and professional lives.

stories.title: Nic Nemeth becomes double champion at TNA Lockdown; Leon Slater invokes Option C for BFG
stories.tldr: At TNA Lockdown, Nic Nemeth became a double champion after he and his brother Ryan defeated The Hardys to win the TNA World Tag Team Championship, adding to his ongoing TNA World Championship reign. Earlier in the night, Leon Slater successfully defeated Cedric Alexander in a brutal Last Man Standing match to regain the X Division Championship. Immediately following the main event, Slater interrupted the Nemeths' celebration to exercise Option C, voluntarily relinquishing the X Division title to TNA President Carlos Silva. Slater then laid down the challenge to face Nic Nemeth for the TNA World Championship at Bound for Glory on October 11 in Tampa, Florida, standing tall over both Nemeth brothers to close the show.

stories.title: Kiera Hogan returns to TNA at Lockdown and wins Knockouts Tag Title with Allie
stories.tldr: Kiera Hogan made a surprise return to TNA at the Lockdown 2026 pay-per-view after a five-year absence. Stepping in as a replacement partner for the absent Rosemary, Hogan helped Allie defeat The Elegance Brand to capture the Knockouts World Tag Team Championships. TNA subsequently confirmed that Hogan has officially signed a new multi-year contract with the company.

stories.title: TNA Lockdown 2026 overall review and results
stories.tldr: TNA recently presented Lockdown 2026 in Chicago, marking the company's first all-cage pay-per-view in a decade. The event featured intense violence, multiple title changes, and dramatic moments including Mustafa Ali's cruel tactics against Jason Hotch and Xia Brookside retaining her championship in a brutal bout. The night culminated with X Division champion Leon Slater laying out the tag team champions and officially cashing in Option C to challenge for the world title at Bound for Glory.

stories.title: Leon Slater defeats Cedric Alexander to win TNA X-Division Title at Lockdown
stories.tldr: Leon Slater defeated Cedric Alexander in a brutal Last Man Standing steel cage match at TNA Lockdown to capture his second X-Division Championship. The high-stakes bout featured severe punishment, including Alexander driving Slater head-first into the cage and delivering an avalanche Michinoku Driver. Slater ultimately turned the tide by hitting three consecutive Lumbar Checks followed by a Swanton 450 to keep Alexander down for the ten-count. The victory not only secures Slater his second title reign but also preserves his historical accolades in TNA, as a loss would have erased his previous records from the history books.

stories.title: Matches set and added for upcoming TNA iMPACT episode
stories.tldr: TNA Wrestling has loaded up the card for the upcoming August 27 episode of iMPACT following events at TNA Lockdown. Two major matches have now been officially locked in for the broadcast, giving fans plenty of reasons to tune in. The updated lineup features a high-stakes championship final as well as an intriguing tag team encounter involving newly crowned gold.

stories.title: Lucha Libre veteran Solar II passes away at age 66
stories.tldr: Lucha libre veteran Solar II, whose real name was Pedro Buenrostro Gomez, has passed away at the age of 66 following recent health struggles. His brother, Solar I, confirmed the sad news in a heartfelt family statement remembering his life and career. Throughout a professional journey spanning over five decades beginning in 1975, he primarily competed for CMLL and captured the NWA World Welterweight Championship in 1988 before retiring in 2002. CMLL honored the late luchador with a moment of silence and applause at Arena Mexico following his passing on August 23.

stories.title: TNA Wrestling holds preliminary investment talks with RARESTNDRD
stories.tldr: TNA Wrestling recently hosted high-profile entertainment and investment figures during the Lockdown 2026 pay-per-view in Chicago to discuss potential strategic partnerships. Nick LoPiccolo, founder of the new venture RARESTNDRD and former Paradigm Talent Agency head, attended the event alongside music executive Brandon Marquez and film producer Tarek Tohme. The preliminary discussions with TNA President Carlos Silva focused on raising capital and potential direct investment into the promotion. LoPiccolo publicly praised the company afterward, emphasizing that he views TNA as a serious growth enterprise rather than a nostalgia act.

stories.title: Matt Hardy reflects on fan support following TNA Lockdown 2026
stories.tldr: Matt Hardy shared a video showing a massive line of fans waiting to meet him and Jeff Hardy over two hours after TNA Lockdown 2026 concluded. Earlier in the night, the legendary tag team main evented the pay-per-view in a brutal steel cage match where they lost the TNA World Tag Team Championships to Nic and Ryan Nemeth. Despite the tough loss and the late hour, the Hardys spent hours signing autographs for a dedicated crowd in Chicago. The impressive turnout highlighted the enduring popularity and massive demand the duo still commands after decades in the wrestling industry.

stories.title: Steph De Lander sparks online debate after insulting biscuits and gravy
stories.tldr: Australian wrestler Steph De Lander sparked a lighthearted online debate after posting on Twitter that biscuits and gravy is an insane American meal. Her comments quickly drew sharp reactions from her peers, including a confused response from Mance Warner. Zachary Wentz strongly defended the Southern comfort food, telling De Lander not to trash the dish. The playful exchange showed just how seriously some wrestlers take their traditional breakfast plates.

stories.title: Elayna Black shows bloody aftermath of TNA Lockdown steel cage match
stories.tldr: Elayna Black failed to capture the Knockouts World Championship from Xia Brookside at TNA Lockdown 2026 after a brutal steel cage match in Chicago. Despite losing following interference and a roll-up, Black shared a graphic mirror selfie on Twitter revealing the extent of her bloody injuries. The controversial hometown loss sparked heavy boos from the live crowd, especially with Black's family watching cageside.

stories.title: DragonKingKarl explores unbroken match lineage from pioneer era
stories.tldr: Wrestling historian Karl Stern recently released a special podcast episode tracing an unbroken match lineage from the pioneer era of the 1800s to the modern rosters of WWE and AEW. The episode serves as both an accessible jumping-on point for new listeners and a thrilling deep dive for longtime fans of early pro wrestling history. By connecting historic figures like Col. James H. McLaughlin directly to contemporary superstars, the audio show argues that pioneer-era wrestling is the true ancestor of today's sports entertainment rather than mixed martial arts.

stories.title: TNA Lockdown 2026 fallout: New champions, returns, and news roundups
stories.tldr: TNA Lockdown 2026 delivered massive fallout featuring multiple new champions and high-profile returns. Mustafa Ali, Leon Slater, and The Nemeth Brothers all captured gold, while Kiera Hogan made her official return and signing with the company. Additionally, Avery Styles, the son of AJ Styles, officially signed with TNA, and the main event set up a blockbuster World Championship match for Bound for Glory.

stories.title: Jason Hotch coughs blood following wild spot at TNA Lockdown
stories.tldr: During a brutal TNA Lockdown match, Jason Hotch defended his TNA International Championship against Mustafa Ali in a chaotic steel cage encounter. The match featured a terrifying high-risk spot where Hotch crashed off the top of the cage and put Ali through a ringside table, resulting in Hotch coughing up blood and sparking fears of internal injuries. Despite the medical scare, Ali escalated the drama by taunting Hotch's family at ringside and destroying a toy belonging to Hotch's daughter. Ali ultimately capitalized on the carnage to secure the victory with back-to-back 450 splashes, though Hotch earned a standing ovation from the crowd for his courageous performance.

stories.title: Mustafa Ali regains TNA International Title at Lockdown in cage match
stories.tldr: Mustafa Ali reclaimed the TNA International Championship by defeating his former Order 4 soldier Jason Hotch in a brutal steel cage match at TNA Lockdown. The hometown bout featured high-risk maneuvers, outside interference from Tasha Steelz and Mila Moore, and psychological warfare involving Hotch's family. Ali ultimately secured the victory and his second title reign after executing two consecutive 450 splashes.

stories.title: Xia Brookside retains TNA Knockouts World Championship at Lockdown
stories.tldr: Xia Brookside successfully defended her TNA Knockouts World Championship against Elayna Black in a brutal match at Lockdown. The champion resorted to underhanded tactics, including using a belt as a weapon and throwing chalk dust into her challenger's eyes to secure the winning pinfall. Meanwhile, Indi Hartwell watched the violent encounter closely from backstage, having already established herself as the next challenger for the title.

stories.title: WWE tryout attendees spotted backstage at TNA Lockdown
stories.tldr: Independent wrestlers J-Rod and Josh Bishop were spotted in attendance at the TNA Lockdown event in Chicago after recently participating in WWE tryouts earlier this month. Both athletes have drawn interest from TNA Wrestling over the past few months, and the promotion is reportedly considering contract offers if they do not sign with WWE. The wrestlers were strictly at the event as spectators and were not dressed to compete. Another independent wrestler, Pinky Montoya, was also spotted attending the show.

stories.title: Candice Michelle makes surprise appearance at TNA Lockdown
stories.tldr: Former WWE Women’s Champion Candice Michelle made a surprise cameo appearance during the Countdown to TNA Lockdown pre-show alongside Daria Rae, Matthew Rehwoldt, and Tom Hannifan. During her appearance, she previewed the Knockouts World Championship match between Xia Brookside and Elayna Black while discussing her backstage producer role with the company. Candice revealed she has been working with TNA since March and recently hinted at a potential in-ring return.

stories.title: Indie veteran Eric Draven reflects on 35-year wrestling career
stories.tldr: Independent wrestling veteran Eric Draven is reflecting on an impressive 35-year career that has spanned 48 states and featured matches against legendary opponents. Trained by wrestling greats like Jeff Jarrett and Rip Rogers, Draven developed his ring name from Jarrett's advice rather than the movie The Crow. Today, the Supreme Wrestling promoter and trainer balances his in-ring experience as an old-school brawler with passing his knowledge down to new talent. As he continues his decades-long journey, Draven remains motivated and active within the independent circuit.

stories.title: Matt Hardy discusses how he would guide his children entering pro wrestling
stories.tldr: TNA star Matt Hardy recently discussed on his podcast how he would approach his three sons potentially entering the professional wrestling business. While fans might love the idea of a second-generation Hardy Boyz team, Matt would take a cautious and calculated approach to their training and career development. He outlined plans to ensure they learn the ins and outs of the industry, start small in independent promotions, and network effectively while preparing for inevitable internet criticism.

stories.title: AJ Styles' son Avery Styles officially signs with TNA Wrestling at Lockdown
stories.tldr: Avery Styles officially signed with TNA Wrestling during the Lockdown pay-per-view event in Chicago. Entering to his father's theme music, the rookie announced his new contract live to the fans. He was immediately confronted and welcomed by Frankie Kazarian, who offered himself as a trustworthy mentor in the locker room.

stories.title: Joe Alonzo signs with TNA Wrestling following Lockdown dark match win
stories.tldr: Following Santino Marella's initial challenge, Joe Alonzo officially secured his TNA Wrestling contract at Lockdown. During the event, the AAW Heavyweight Champion defeated the masked Home Town Man in a dark match stipulation to cement his new status. Reports indicate that Alonzo's deal was actually finalized prior to the match following a series of impressive independent appearances.

stories.title: DREAM Pro Wrestling raises funds for Rebel's ALS fight
stories.tldr: DREAM Pro Wrestling recently raised over seven thousand dollars for Tanea Brooks, known as Rebel, following her ALS diagnosis earlier this year. The promotion held a special benefit show organized by Truth Magnum of The Outrunners to support her ongoing battle against the terminal illness. Additionally, AEW is stepping up its support by hosting a dedicated episode of Dynamite titled Rebel Heart in Athens, Georgia. The upcoming event highlights the continued solidarity from the wrestling community toward the former star.
